reason: I’ll start with the wet food remainder and microbes to see how the community uses what digestion left behind.
expectation: I expect the microbes to act on some of the undigested material, perhaps producing substances the body can use.

alternatives.reason: The mucus may establish the habitat, but I want to follow the meal first.

effect: Fermentation produces small fatty acids and gas, so I’ll connect those contents to the body to follow their effects.
reaction: The reminder that microbes differ adds useful nuance.
reason: Connecting the fermenting contents to the body may show what happens to the products.
expectation: I expect to see an exchange between the colon and the body, perhaps absorption of some fatty acids.

alternatives.reason: Mucus may clarify the habitat, but I want to follow the fermentation products first.

effect: The picture shows fatty acids entering lining cells and blood, while water and salts move toward capillaries. The remaining step is to add mucus.
reaction: The arrows make the exchanges clear, though the fatty acids’ uses remain unexplained.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should add the colon’s mucus layer to the model.
expectation: I expect mucus to appear on the colon lining, showing how it relates to the microbes and intestinal cells.

effect: The completed model shows mucus separating most bacteria from the lining and explains that colon cells can use some microbial fatty acids; others enter blood.
reaction: That answered my question about the fatty acids and made the exchanges feel more complete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fermenting the food remainder and following its products into the colon made the microbial community’s connection to the body concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: The intermediate body-with-contents picture largely repeated the fermentation result, although its exchange arrows added useful information.

surprise.text: Some microbial fatty acids enter lining cells and can be used by them, while others enter blood.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless; adding mucus was the only offered combination at that point, and its separating role became clear in the result.

continue.text: I would continue: the compact sequence connected microbial fermentation, absorption and the mucus barrier, though the compatible-option menu made the choices fairly straightforward.
